attacks.claim: The rollback path does not reconcile suppression state from the Ghost era. Unsubscribes, bounces, and complaints recorded in Ghost during the first weeks of sending are not written back to MailPoet, so re-enabling MailPoet could re-mail people who already opted out. Once Ghost has sent to 46k subscribers, those sends cannot be undone.
attacks.evidence: "rollback = repoint DNS and re-enable MailPoet sending, with any new Ghost signups exported and re-imported to MailPoet." Signups are covered, but ABSENT: any reverse sync of unsubscribes, bounces, or complaints from Ghost to MailPoet. Section 3 covers only the unsubscribe write-back for the Postmark rehearsal, not the production rollback.
